Last Friday (21st), during the Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China trial verdict, in the early hours a police officer took a woman who was queuing for a seat in the public gallery away in a police van. Police responded to inquiries by saying the woman was arrested on three charges, including "behaving in a disorderly manner in a public place," "resisting or intentionally obstructing a police officer in the execution of their duty," and "with seditious intent."

In the early hours of last Friday at around 5 a.m., more than 50 people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. During the queue, a plainclothes police officer pointed out a woman in the line saying her "clothes seemed to have some seditious elements," and took her away in a police van. While the officer was removing the woman, multiple officers repeatedly directed reporters to leave, saying "take you to the press area," and pulled orange cordon lines towards Ying Wa Street. After the woman had boarded the police van, they put away the cordon lines. A "court observer" who was queuing near the woman that day said she was wearing a black T-shirt with Japanese text printed on it.

"集誌社" (Citizen News) inquired with police about the reason the woman was taken away and whether an arrest had been made. Police replied this morning (24th) that during a security operation near the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts on 21 August, they arrested a 45-year-old woman on suspicion of "behaving in a disorderly manner in a public place," "resisting or intentionally obstructing a police officer in the execution of their duty," and "with seditious intent," and she has been detained for investigation.
